description: FORGE is a framework and dataset for industrial control system security research, published on IEEE DataPort in May 2026. The dataset page read on 2026-09-28 explains that it couples MATLAB and Simulink process models with containerised OpenPLC controllers and a human-machine interface on a virtual network, running faster than real time, up to 359 times, while keeping signal correlations above 0.99 against real-time runs. It provides 5,000 benign and 1,000 attack runs across five testbeds: a water storage tank, a two-zone HVAC system, a gas pipeline, a shell-and-tube heat exchanger and an industrial robot arm, with five Modbus attacks labelled by MITRE ATT&CK for ICS techniques; each run has its configuration file, a raw packet capture, synchronised process telemetry and a signed manifest. Coverage is simulated plants, not real sites. Access requires an IEEE DataPort subscription to download the 295 megabyte archive; no licence is stated. Caveats: the testbeds are small idealised processes, and attack variety is limited to five Modbus techniques. It supports cyber resilience studies of water and gas control systems, such as training and testing intrusion detection on a pipeline or tank controller. Related records: the ICS SCADA cyber kit testbed traffic and the ICS-SimLab container simulation.
